notes: Company: global knowledge management platform for enterprise clients (legal + finance verticals). Produces vector index for customer documents, logs, and contracts.
Problem: current vector store (self-hosted Milvus + custom shards) cannot meet cost/latency targets at 400M+ vectors; heavy ops overhead.
Primary ask: commodity cost per query target <$0.001 (including rerank); steady-state QPS 800–1200, burst to 5k for short windows.
Index scale: target initial index 400M vectors, roadmap to 1B+ within 12–18 months. Compression/quantization mandatory.
Latency targets: median retrieval+rerank <200ms for standard queries, p95 <350ms. Rerank uses cross-encoder on GPU on top candidates (top-50).
Deployment constraints: must run inside customer VPC for first three pilot customers; later want Private on-prem package for regulated accounts.
Security: strict KMS integration for embedding keys, audit logs for model access, SOC2 required. Asked about HSM/KMS compatibility — provided redwood-kms-integration.pdf (drive link).
Quote from CTO (02/18 call): "We need unit economics that scale — 1B vectors has to be an order of magnitude cheaper than our current build."

Benchmark note: initial microbench with Redwood hosted endpoint (small subset, 10M vectors equivalent) showed ~45% cost reduction vs current infra and 20% lower median latency using prefix caching + rerank offload strategy.

POC scope: 1) ingest pipeline + incremental indexing (100M subset), 2) measure continuous batching benefits, 3) validate KV/prefix caching to reduce rerank calls, 4) rerank latency with batched cross-encoder on reserved GPU pool.
Docs shared: security questionnaire (Drive), sample data schema, current indexing topology diagram (Milvus shards x16), Jira ticket INF-4321 for indexing bug during ingestion.
Sales note: favorable ARR if Redwood can guarantee throughput SLAs; pricing sensitivity high — prefer predictable reserved capacity with scaling add-on.
